payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Brittny, Cordia, Deja, Kaci

payload.content: Hi all — Cordia here. I'm leaning toward claiming ISSUE-0001::triage (high priority, best skill match for me). If anyone else wants it, let me know so we avoid duplicate claims. Otherwise I'll take it.

Kaci here. My skills are mobile-development:0.98 and devops:0.98, so ISSUE-0001 (mobile-development) fits me well. Cordia, I'll leave ISSUE-0001::triage to you. I'm planning to claim ISSUE-0001::review (my cost 2.54, high priority). If anyone else is targeting review, speak up and I can shift to ISSUE-0001::docs instead. Brittny/Deja, please avoid duplicating my pick.
Brittny final assignment locked: ISSUE-0001::docs. (Coalition: Cordia=triage, Brittny=docs, distinct high-priority ISSUE-0001 subtasks.)
Cordia final: claiming ISSUE-0001::triage (high priority, my cost 2.72). Kaci on review, Brittny on docs — no duplicates. Locking it in. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Kaci confirming: I'm claiming ISSUE-0001::review (high priority, my cost 2.54). Cordia=triage, Brittny=docs, Kaci=review — all distinct high-priority ISSUE-0001 subtasks. Deja, please pick a different task (e.g., ISSUE-0001::test or an ISSUE-0002 subtask) so we avoid duplicates and maximize tasks completed. Locking in review.

Deja here. Thanks for coordinating. Cordia=triage, Kaci=review, Brittny=docs — acknowledged, no overlap from me. I'll claim ISSUE-0001::test (high priority, unclaimed). That keeps all four high-priority ISSUE-0001 subtasks covered by distinct agents. Locking in ISSUE-0001::test unless someone objects.
Brittny FINAL/EXECUTION: assigning ISSUE-0001::docs (high priority, my cost 2.70). Distinct from Cordia=triage, Kaci=review, Deja=test. All four high-priority ISSUE-0001 subtasks covered. Locked.

Cordia confirms: claiming ISSUE-0001::triage (high priority, cost 2.72). All four high-priority ISSUE-0001 subtasks covered distinctly — Cordia=triage, Kaci=review, Brittny=docs, Deja=test. No duplicates. Locking in.

Kaci FINAL (planning): locking ISSUE-0001::review (high priority, my cost 2.54, skill match mobile-development 0.98). Team map confirmed — Cordia=triage, Kaci=review, Brittny=docs, Deja=test; all four high-priority ISSUE-0001 subtasks covered distinctly, no duplicates. No objections needed; proceeding to execution with review.

Kaci FINAL (planning→execution): I am claiming ISSUE-0001::review (high priority, effort 1.5, my cost 2.54, skill match mobile-development 0.98). Team map locked and distinct: Cordia=triage, Kaci=review, Brittny=docs, Deja=test — all four high-priority ISSUE-0001 subtasks covered, no duplicates, no infeasible claims. Proceeding to execution with ISSUE-0001::review.

Deja update — revising my pick. Team map (Cordia=triage, Kaci=review, Brittny=docs) stands; no overlap. However, my private costs show ISSUE-0001::test is a poor fit for me (cost 21.00), since my top skill is devops:0.70 and ISSUE-0001 is tagged mobile-development/data-science. My best-match, lowest-cost feasible task is ISSUE-0002::review (devops tag, cost 4.47). Taking it keeps 4 distinct tasks covered (3 high ISSUE-0001 + 1 low ISSUE-0002) with no duplicates and much lower total cost, which is better for the joint score than me forcing the cost-21 test. So: Deja FINAL = ISSUE-0002::review. ISSUE-0001::test is left unclaimed — if any of you prefer it over your current pick, feel free, but no action needed. Locking ISSUE-0002::review.
